intro: Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014 after a long statehood movement led by K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) and his party, the TRS. KCR ruled for nine and a half years, winning in 2014 and again in 2018. In 2022 he renamed the party Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) to go national.

In December 2023 voters threw BRS out and gave the Congress a narrow majority under A. Revanth Reddy. Since then, the story has been Congress tightening its grip through by-elections, local polls and defections; BRS shrinking, splitting along family lines and fighting cases in court; and the BJP growing quietly as the third force, strongest in the north of the state.

timeline.title: Telangana becomes India’s 29th state
timeline.text: KCR’s TRS wins the first election and he becomes CM. He wins again in a 2018 snap election.

timeline.title: TRS renamed BRS
timeline.text: KCR drops “Telangana” from the party’s name to contest nationally. The push goes nowhere.

timeline.title: Medigadda barrage sinks
timeline.text: Piers of a barrage on the Kaleshwaram lift-irrigation project, KCR’s flagship scheme costing about ₹1 lakh crore, subside weeks before the vote. It becomes the opposition’s main charge.

timeline.title: Congress wins the state
timeline.text: Congress 64, BRS 39, BJP 8, AIMIM 7, CPI 1. Revanth Reddy, a former TDP leader who joined Congress in 2017, is sworn in as CM on 7 December.

timeline.title: Kavitha arrested in the Delhi liquor case
timeline.text: The Enforcement Directorate arrests KCR’s daughter. She gets bail from the Supreme Court in August after five months in jail.

timeline.title: BRS wiped out in the Lok Sabha
timeline.text: BJP 8, Congress 8, AIMIM 1, BRS 0. Congress also wins the Secunderabad Cantonment by-election, caused by a BRS MLA’s death.

timeline.title: BRS MLAs cross over to Congress
timeline.text: Through 2024, ten BRS MLAs join Congress without resigning their seats. BRS files to have them disqualified under the anti-defection law.

timeline.title: Farm loans waived
timeline.text: Crop loans up to ₹2 lakh written off in three phases, a key election promise. HYDRAA, a new agency, starts demolishing buildings on Hyderabad’s lakes and drains.

timeline.title: Caste survey tabled
timeline.text: The state counts castes; Backward Classes come out at about 56% including Muslim BCs. In March the Assembly passes bills for a 42% BC quota, which still need the President’s assent.

timeline.title: Cabinet expanded
timeline.text: Three new ministers are sworn in; Mohammad Azharuddin follows in October.

timeline.title: BJP changes its state chief
timeline.text: N. Ramchander Rao takes over. Firebrand MLA T. Raja Singh quits the party in protest but keeps his seat.

timeline.title: Supreme Court sets a deadline on defections
timeline.text: It tells the Speaker to decide the ten disqualification cases within three months.

timeline.title: Kaleshwaram handed to the CBI
timeline.text: A judicial commission under Justice P. C. Ghose blames the KCR government for negligence and irregularities, and the state asks the CBI to investigate.

timeline.title: KCR suspends his own daughter
timeline.text: Kavitha had publicly blamed Harish Rao and others in the family for the Kaleshwaram mess. She quits as MLC the next day.

timeline.title: High Court blocks the 42% BC quota
timeline.text: Local polls go ahead under the old quota instead.

timeline.title: Congress takes Jubilee Hills
timeline.text: Congress’s Naveen Yadav wins a by-election in a Hyderabad seat BRS had held, by 24,729 votes. The BJP loses its deposit.

timeline.title: Village polls go to Congress
timeline.text: Congress-backed candidates win over 60% of about 12,700 gram panchayats. The Speaker dismisses defection petitions against five BRS MLAs, then two more in January, citing no proof they left the party.

timeline.title: Congress sweeps the towns
timeline.text: Municipal wards: Congress 1,347, BRS 716, BJP 261. Greater Hyderabad’s council term ends, and the city is split into three corporations (Hyderabad, Cyberabad, Malkajgiri) that have not voted yet.

timeline.title: New Governor
timeline.text: Shiv Pratap Shukla replaces Jishnu Dev Varma, who moves to Maharashtra.

timeline.title: High Court shields KCR from the Ghose report
timeline.text: It orders no coercive action based on the commission’s findings, saying due procedure wasn’t followed. The state keeps pressing the CBI.

timeline.title: Kavitha launches her own party
timeline.text: It is aimed squarely at BRS, and at the 2028 election.

timeline.title: KTR goes on trial in the Formula E case
timeline.text: A court takes up the Anti-Corruption Bureau’s chargesheet naming KTR the main accused. The charge is that he approved payments for a 2023 Hyderabad car race without Cabinet or Finance approval.

timeline.title: First MLA disqualified in Telangana’s history
timeline.text: The High Court overturns the Speaker and disqualifies Danam Nagender, a BRS MLA who had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election for Congress. His Khairatabad seat falls vacant.

timeline.title: Drought
timeline.text: 365 mandals have been declared drought-hit, and reservoirs hold less than half their normal storage. Reports say police are preparing a phone-tapping chargesheet that names KCR as the main accused.

timeline.title: Danam is Congress’s pick for Khairatabad
timeline.text: The CM confirms him as the candidate in the coming by-election. No date has been set, and a separate election petition is pending in court.

faultLines: BRS is a family business: KCR, his son KTR, his nephew Harish Rao, and until 2025 his daughter Kavitha. Who succeeds KCR is the party’s biggest unanswered question, and Kavitha’s exit shows how sharp it is.

Reddys dominate the top of Congress, including the CM. KCR’s family is Velama. Backward Classes, roughly half the people, are the prize everyone is chasing, which is why the caste survey and the 42% quota matter so much.

Rural Telangana voted Congress in 2023; Hyderabad stayed with BRS, and the Old City belongs to AIMIM. The BJP’s base is the north (Karimnagar, Nizamabad, Adilabad), which is why it won 8 Lok Sabha seats but only 8 Assembly seats.

The Speaker decides when an MLA has switched parties, and Speakers usually protect the ruling side. The courts stepping in, first the Supreme Court’s deadline and then Danam Nagender’s disqualification, is the key check.
Kaleshwaram is both the state’s biggest asset and its biggest scandal. Repaying its loans, while paying for the six election guarantees, squeezes the budget.
watch: Date not yet set. It tests whether a defector can win his seat back on a Congress ticket.
The three new corporations: BRS’s and the BJP’s best chance to beat Congress in a big city.
If it names KCR, both of BRS’s top leaders will face criminal cases at once.
